R-security-1 (GET /invoices/:id returns any organization's invoice) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.recommendation: Insecure direct object reference (CWE-639 / CWE-862). Any authenticated user of organization 7 who sends `GET /invoices/42` receives invoice 42 even when it belongs to another organization, and can enumerate every invoice by iterating ids. Scope the query to the caller, as the list route does — `WHERE id = $1 AND org_id = $2` with `[id, currentUser(req).orgId]` — and answer 404 when no row matches, so existence in another organization is not revealed. Add a test that a caller of another organization gets 404.
findings.title: GET /invoices/:id returns any organization's invoice

findings.recommendation: Information exposure through an error message (CWE-209). Any request whose handler throws — a database failure in `query`, a driver error quoting the SQL or the connection details — returns the raw message and the full stack trace (file paths, module layout, library versions) to the caller. Keep `console.error(err)` on the server and answer a generic body such as `{ error: "internal error" }`.
findings.title: The error handler sends the error message and stack trace to the client

findings.recommendation: `Number(" ")` is 0 and `Number("1e3")` is 1000, so whitespace or exponent forms pass the integer check. No data is exposed by it, but an allow-list at the boundary is stricter: accept only `/^[1-9]\d*$/` and answer 400 otherwise.
findings.title: An empty or zero id passes the id validation
